jurisdiction.name: Angola
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Angola has no adopted AI law or AI strategy, but several drafts are in public consultation: the telecommunications and ICT ministry's (MINTTICS) full draft AI Law of September 2025, with risk duties, stricter rules for critical, public-sector, judicial, medical and biometric AI and a new AI authority; the data protection agency's draft revision of the data protection law adding AI prohibitions and rights; and a 2026 draft Digital Government Law setting rules for AI in public administration. The 2011 data protection law (Law 22/11) already restricts automated individual decisions, and a national AI strategy and a public-sector AI framework are being prepared.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Telecommunications, Information Technologies and Social Communication (MINTTICS)
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The official gazette could not be accessed, and the national AI strategy is still being prepared and is listed as a lead. As a country of over 20 million people with few records, Angola is marked for a longer catch-up pass.

instruments.official_title: Proposta de Lei sobre a Inteligência Artificial
instruments.english_title: Draft Law on Artificial Intelligence (public-consultation version)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Telecommunications, Information Technologies and Social Communication (MINTTICS), as proponent
instruments.current_status: Draft bill dated 'Luanda, Setembro de 2025' published for public consultation on the MINTTICS consultation portal (consultapublica.minttics.gov.ao), where it remains the featured consultation; the portal does not state opening/closing dates. Not yet submitted to or approved by the National Assembly as of 12 October 2026 (no gazette publication found).
instruments.summary: A 86-article draft general AI law proposed by MINTTICS, preceded by a justification report with a comparative study (US, EU, China, Japan, Canada, Brazil, Africa). It sets AI principles, user rights (information, explanation and refusal of AI-based decisions, complaints), safety, risk-assessment, incident-reporting and AI-content labelling duties for developers and providers, a stricter regime for 'critical AI' (registration, risk assessment, emergency response), and special rules for AI use by the State and public administration, judicial, news and medical AI, social bots, biometric recognition, autonomous driving and general-purpose AI. It provides for an AI competent authority to be created by regulation, an expert commission, administrative offences, AI crimes, strict civil liability and pilot supervision mechanisms.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Angola's first draft horizontal AI law; would create a dedicated AI regulator.
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Telecommunications, Information Technologies and Social Communication

instruments.official_title: Projecto de Revisão da Lei n.º 22/11, de 17 de Junho - Lei de Protecção de Dados Pessoais
instruments.english_title: Draft Revision of Law No. 22/11 of 17 June - Personal Data Protection Law (public-consultation version)
instruments.issuing_authority: Data Protection Agency (Agência de Protecção de Dados, APD)
instruments.current_status: Put to public consultation by the APD on the government consultation portal from 17 March to 17 April 2025 (status 'Encerrada'). Not adopted as of 12 October 2026 (no gazette publication found); Law 22/11 remains in force.
instruments.summary: Draft replacement of Angola's 2011 data protection law put to consultation by the APD. Besides a right not to be subject to solely automated or semi-automated decisions, it adds a section on processing personal data by AI systems: it bans AI that manipulates people into compromising privacy, exploits vulnerabilities of specific groups, or performs social scoring leading to unfavourable treatment. It gives data subjects affected by AI rights to prior information, explanation, contestation and human participation, and requires AI producers, providers and operators to adopt governance and data-management practices against discrimination.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Would introduce AI-specific prohibitions and data-subject rights into Angolan data protection law.

instruments.official_title: Ante-Projecto de Proposta de Lei do Governo Digital
instruments.issuing_authority: Administrative Modernisation Institute (Instituto de Modernização Administrativa, IMA), Presidency of the Republic
instruments.current_status: Preliminary draft (cover dated Luanda, 2 April 2026) put to public consultation by the IMA on the government consultation portal from 6 May to 7 June 2026 (status 'Encerrada'). Not adopted as of 12 October 2026.
instruments.summary: Draft framework law on digital government covering digital public services, electronic administrative procedure, digital identity, public-data governance, interoperability and the use of automated systems and AI in public administration. It subjects public-sector AI to legality, necessity, proportionality, transparency, explainability, non-discrimination, human oversight and accountability, bans AI for indiscriminate mass surveillance, unlawful profiling or arbitrary discrimination, and requires prior impact and risk assessment, an institutional register, technical documentation and audit records for AI used in relevant administrative functions. The administration remains liable for errors caused by data, design, bias or insufficient oversight.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Would set binding rules for AI use by Angolan public administration.

instruments.official_title: Lei n.º 22/11, de 17 de Junho - Lei da Protecção de Dados Pessoais
instruments.english_title: Law No. 22/11 of 17 June 2011 on the Protection of Personal Data
instruments.current_status: In force since publication in Diário da República I Série n.º 114 of 17 June 2011 (art. 67). A full revision prepared by the Data Protection Agency was put to public consultation in March-April 2025 and was not yet adopted as of 12 October 2026.
instruments.summary: Angola's general personal data protection law, applying to wholly or partly automated processing of personal data and supervised by the Data Protection Agency. Its art. 29 gives every person the right not to be subject to a decision producing legal or similarly significant effects based solely on automated processing intended to evaluate personal aspects such as professional capacity, creditworthiness, reliability or conduct, with exceptions for contracts with safeguards and cases authorised by the Agency with safeguards defined by it.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: The only binding Angolan rule found that directly governs automated (algorithmic) decision-making.
